From research and speaker acquisition to the shop floor at Amac.

about.title: Where people and technology meet
paragraphs: I'm Robert Karzijn. My interest is at the intersection of people and technology: how people use interfaces, which habits form along the way and how design (deliberately or not) plays into that. In my bachelor's thesis I experimentally investigated how web shops can disrupt procedural memory by relocating interface elements.

Alongside my studies I work parttime at Amac in Apeldoorn, where I progressed from Junior Sales Associate to Senior Sales Associate with Daily Operations Lead in two years and worked across several branches to share knowledge and experience. That combination keeps me sharp: theory on user behaviour in the lecture hall, and real users in front of me on the shop floor parttime.
I'm currently following a master's in Human-Computer Interaction. Outside study and work: photography, going to the gym and the occasional evening of gaming.

items.name: Research
items.promise: Finding out how people actually behave, not how we assume they do.
items.text: From literature review and experimental design to data collection and statistical analysis. In my bachelor's thesis I studied with 40 participants how relocating interface elements disrupts habitual behaviour in web shops.

items.name: Design
items.promise: Interfaces that do what you expect.
items.text: Translating requirements into a design, and that design into something that works. I designed and built MobiPad myself: from requirements and architecture to three controller layouts, tested on real hardware.

items.name: Organise
items.promise: Bringing people, plans and agreements together, against a deadline.
items.text: Recruiting and supporting speakers for exec(ut), keeping daily operations running at Amac as Daily Operations Lead, and keeping the administration of Stichting Sticky as its secretary.
